subject: DPA clarifications & next steps after call
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@auroratech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Wong <j.wong@auroratech.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: DPA questions and next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning - helpful to walk through Redwood's architecture and options. A few follow-ups from our legal and security teams so we can scope the procurement timeline: 

1) Controller / Processor roles: Can you confirm Redwood's position in the DPA? From the call we heard Redwood will be the processor and Aurora Tech the controller, but our legal team wants that explicit.

2) Subprocessors: Please share the current subprocessor list and confirm the notice process for adding new subprocessors (how much advance notice). Also: do you have any subprocessors located in China or other APAC regions? We need to ensure no unauthorized data routing outside EU/US for certain data classes.

3) Breach notice timing: What is Redwood's standard SLA for breach notifications? Our procurement would prefer 'as soon as reasonably practicable' with a contractual maximum (48 hours for incidents involving PII). Is that negotiable?

4) Data retention and logging: What are the default retention windows for request logs, prompts, and generated outputs? Can retention be configured per-customer or per-deployment (hosted vs. dedicated/private)?

5) Data residency: We intend to keep all PII and model inputs/responses within EU regions. Can you confirm hosted EU-only options and whether subprocessors for hosted EU can be restricted?

Please send relevant artifacts (DPA redline, SOC 2 attestation, current subprocessor list). Our legal would like to turn this around within two weeks if possible.

Appreciate it -
Samantha
Head of Security & Privacy, Aurora Tech

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@auroratech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA questions and next steps

Hi Samantha - great to talk this morning. Short answers first, then next steps: 

- Controller/Processor: Redwood is the processor; Aurora Tech is the controller. We'll include that language explicitly in the DPA addendum.

- Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessor list (subprocessors_list_20270311.csv). We provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors as standard; in cases where customers require stricter controls we can discuss contractual notice or carve-outs. None of the subprocessors on the current list are based in mainland China.

- Breach notice: Our standard practice is to notify customers as soon as reasonably practicable and provide initial notification within 72 hours for incidents that materially affect customer data. We are open to contract language that tightens this (see below).

- Data retention & logging: Default request/log retention for hosted accounts is 90 days for request metadata and 30 days for full prompt/response storage by default. For Dedicated/Private deployments retention is configurable and can be set to comply with customer retention policies.

- Data residency: We support EU-hosted deployments with EU-only processing for customers electing EU region. For Hosted EU customers we can commit to processing/storage in EU regions and restrict cross-region failover unless explicitly authorized. Dedicated/Private deployments give you full control over residency.

Next steps: 
1) I'm attaching a DPA addendum redline (DPA_Addendum_redline_v1.pdf), our latest SOC 2 attestation (SOC2_Attestation_2026.pdf), and the subprocessor list referenced above.
2) If Aurora wants to tighten breach notification to 48 hours for PII incidents, we can propose language: "Redwood will notify Controller as soon as reasonably practicable and no later than forty-eight (48) hours for Security Incidents involving Customer PII."
3) Ben and Dev are copied - Ben can own the contractual thread and I can loop in Legal for a formal redline.

If helpful, we can schedule a short call with our privacy counsel. DocuSign draft link is included below for convenience.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_redline_v1.pdf, SOC2_Attestation_2026.pdf, subprocessors_list_20270311.csv

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@auroratech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Wong <j.wong@auroratech.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 16:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA questions and next steps

Thanks Marissa - quick clarification: 

- The 72 -> 48 hour change you proposed is helpful. Can you confirm you can accept 48 hours specifically for incidents involving customer PII? We need that in writing for our board.

- Regarding subprocessors: Aurora needs to avoid any new subprocessors outside EU/US for the next 12 months for workloads that will process PII. If that requires a carve-out or an additional clause (e.g., "Customer may restrict subprocessors by geography for specific accounts"), please propose language.

If you can send the updated DPA wording and confirm the subprocessor geography restriction options, we can have legal review and aim to sign within the two-week window.

Samantha

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@auroratech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA questions and next steps

Samantha - appreciate the clarity. Quick note from our side on the two asks: 

1) Breach notification timing: We are prepared to accept the proposed contractual language to make the 48-hour cap explicit for incidents involving customer PII: "Redwood will notify Controller as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event no later than forty-eight (48) hours following confirmation that Customer PII has been impacted." Our legal will include that in the DPA redline.

2) Subprocessor geography restrictions: For Hosted customers we can commit to EU/US-only subprocessors for specified accounts for a 12-month period, and we will include a clause that allows Aurora to opt into a "geography-restricted" subprocessor list. For Dedicated/Private deployments this is naturally enforced by residency choices.

Next step: Marissa and I will update the redline to reflect both items and re-send. If it looks good to Aurora legal we can send a DocuSign for signature. I dropped the DocuSign draft link in the related links.

Would you like a short call Monday to finalize language?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
